findings: Non-blocking (privacy/doc contradiction): human_controls.py's module docstring states 'Original agent protocols, prompts and partial outputs never enter Actions artifacts', but execute() includes prompt_<stage>.md files (full stage bodies with the entire bound context) in evidence.json's original_system_records; the records filter only excludes runner_* files. Content is repo-derived, DANGER-screened and size-capped, so no concrete new exposure at this commit, but either exclude prompt_* from the records collection (as the answer-assembly already does) or correct the docstring/HUMAN_CONTROLS.md invariant.

Non-blocking (state leak): actions_runner.system_stage restores sc.STATE only when old_state is not None; if the scout module had no STATE attribute, it is left permanently pointing at the deleted temp workdir after the call. Restore or delete the attribute unconditionally in the finally block.
Non-blocking (dead code): the local 'config' dict in actions_runner.system_stage is never used; the TOML profile string is what is written to AGENTS.toml.

Non-blocking (recovery semantics): restore() reads a single artifact-listing page (per_page=100, no pagination). More than 100 same-name artifacts silently falls through to a fresh execution instead of replay — the safe direction given the documented caps, but worth knowing.

Accepted limitation (trust boundary): reviewed() enforces adapter-review integrity via unsigned committed hash records (execution.json/response.json); anyone with write access to the two allowed branches could regenerate both records and the reviewed files together. Enforcement rests on branch protection and PR review, not cryptographic signing.

Defense-in-depth (unverifiable pins): tool-free enforcement for the claude family relies entirely on pinned CLI flags (--tools '', strict empty MCP config, --permission-mode dontAsk) against CLI version 2.1.222, which cannot be verified source-only; unlike the codex path there is no post-hoc protocol-event scan raising UNEXPECTED_MODEL_TOOL_USE. An invalid flag fails closed to MODEL_EXECUTION_FAILED, but a silently ignored flag would go undetected — consider adding a claude-side event scan symmetric to codex's.

Verified: artifact export is validated (exact file set, symlink/size/DANGER/hash checks) before the artifact name reaches GITHUB_OUTPUT, so upload cannot fire on unvalidated content; replay requires exact source SHA, originating control workflow path, workflow_dispatch provenance, and byte-hash matches, with all checks preceding any write; interpret hard-blocks; all receipts record human_ratification=False and patient_execution=False; grounding() enforces the predecessor interpretation hash chain; workflows are contents:read with persist-credentials:false and no Git publication path.
